Per-writer tests that DO exist (informational; do NOT cite them for this single-clause criterion): CMS-03C-04 locale_variant/004-relay-source-race-grants.sqlinc:95-122 (lock position 4 FOR SHARE; deadlock and lock-acquisition failure converted to the typed retryable CONFLICT; control: other failures not converted; all tagged AC-276) plus apps/worker/src/cms-composition-production-locale.test.ts:461 "[P2-S12-AC-276] maps the typed retryable CONFLICT of a residual deadlock to the 409 locale catalog code"; CMS-03C-05 related_content/007-cas-and-locks.sqlinc:46 and :48 (static lock order 0,1,2..; transport converts deadlock/lock timeout to 409 RELATED_CONTENT_VERSION_CONFLICT); CMS-03C-15 pattern_updates/080-lock-order.sqlinc (source positions 0 < 1 < 3 < 4 < 5, each occurring once); the linked scan (positions 0,3,4,5); the recheck run (governed_recheck/070-isolation and 075-digest-locks, DEC-221: lock_not_available and deadlock_detected are the typed retryable CONFLICT for the activation and decision rechecks); governed_activation/090-lineage-lock.sqlinc (lineage advisory lock for activate/retire); taxonomy_terms/094-continuation-authority (the merge continuation re-proves curator capability under the position 1 locks); pattern_placement/070-supersede (pinned definitions, rule 2); race_fixes_pattern_locks.sql (position-3 helper, catalog level only) with dec199_publication.race.mjs (publication versus nested pattern activation).

Confirmed absent: lock-order and deadlock/lock-failure tests for CMS-03C-01, -02 (a table lock oracle only), -03, -06, -07, -08, -09 (lineage lock only), -12, -16, CMS-03C-19 claim/execute order, the revision-append carry-over (grep of dec193_carry for lock/deadlock finds none) and the term-merge COMMAND (080-merge.sqlinc quotes "FOR UPDATE in id order" in a comment and asserts behaviour, not order). Also no test shows "the same Idempotency-Key reusable" after a lock failure for any writer except through the generic idempotency suites.

Unverified is correct. The eight scenarios are one list under one predicate ("each have a deterministic tested outcome"), so a verbatim split cannot credit the covered ones; the clause is proven only when all eight are.

Scenarios 7 and 8 have no Slice 12 test at all: grep of supabase/tests/phase_02_slice_12* for "lease" finds only the leaseId plumbing of the schedule claim (no lease-expiry or re-claim assertion), and "restore epoch" appears only in the platform recovery suites (persistence_authority, recovery_readiness_authority), never in a CMS writer. These two make a verified status impossible without new tests.

Scenarios 1-6 have deterministic SEQUENTIAL tests of one commit order, not a two-session race for the exact pair (informational; do NOT cite them for the single clause): (1) activation versus block withdrawal: governed_activation/060-invalidation "a changed frozen dependency commits the invalidation and answers the dependency_changed refusal envelope for activate and for schedule [P2-S12-AC-084]" and governed_recheck/050-block "after the withdrawal the recheck invalidates the review dependency_changed [P2-S12-AC-202]"; (2) linked update versus local override: the diff_has_collisions and collision-choice tests (sequential); dec193_writer.race is accept versus target ACTIVATION, a different pair; (3) term merge versus assignment: taxonomy_terms/080-merge (assignments re-pointed by appended versions) and the dec194 sweep/outer races (recovery versus a producer), not a new assignment racing a merge; (4) locale_variant/004 "a translation of a superseded source revision is the 409 conflict: the source edit won [P2-S12-AC-277]" and "the refused translation wrote no variant, revision or event [P2-S12-AC-277]" (the only AC-277-tagged tests; one commit order); (5) related target unpublish: restore_relation_visibility race is restore versus relation visibility; (6) duplicate and out-of-order events: outbox idempotency suites exist but no Slice 12 redelivery/ordering test for the cms.template/pattern/localization events.

Decision for the owner, not the lane: whether "deterministic tested outcome" means a two-session race per pair (the lane's reading, which the criterion title "Concurrency scenarios" supports) or a pinned outcome per commit order (which would let scenarios 1-4 close with sequential tests). Under either reading 7 and 8 are open.
